newsitem.title: UK: British public borrowing soars in August.
newsitem.headline: British public borrowing soars in August.

text.p: The British government was forced to borrow 4.5 billion pounds in August to make up the shortfall between public spending and tax receipts, the Office for National Statistics (ONS) said on Tuesday.
This compares with a surplus of 1.66 billion pounds in July and brought the total for the first five months of the tax year to 13.37 billion stg compared with 16.72 for the same period last year.

The Treasury shrugged off the sharp increase in borrowing, a spokesman saying figures published in recent months were consistent with the government hitting its borrowing forecast of 27 billion pounds in the fiscal year.
Analysts called the August figures disappointing, however.
They said the figures reduced the scope for tax cuts this year, although most still expected Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke to include some income tax cuts in the November budget.
